drhp.business: ESAB India Limited operates in the fabrication segment, where all its key product categories are sold through a strong and growing distribution network and, increasingly, exported. Alongside products, the Company runs support services — a GCC and R&D services rendered to related parties — which saw double-digit growth and new workstreams during the year. It is a subsidiary of a US listed entity, with ESAB Corporation, Delaware, USA as its ultimate parent, and has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company of its own.

drhp.expansion: The annual report discloses no named expansion project, no new plant and no capacity-addition timeline. Capital expenditure during 2025-26 was primarily on infrastructure — including buildings, EHS and R&D — and on refurbishments of existing lines, and was directed towards productivity improvements, marginal capacity enhancements and upgrading IT systems. There is therefore no step-change capacity programme underway; the spend is maintenance-and-productivity in character, with only 'marginal capacity enhancements' claimed. risks.note: Explicitly named first among key risks in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns'; with input costs rising, pricing pressure compresses the ability to pass through commodity and energy inflation.

A continued surge in commodity prices along with increased energy costs and a weaker Rupee in the last quarter posed significant challenges to profitability; the Company uses export growth to offset some of the FX risk on imports.
risks.risk: Input cost and currency exposure (commodities, energy, weaker Rupee on imports)

risks.note: Supply-chain driven issues on working capital are flagged as a key risk; management's stated response is de-risking the supply chain to hold service levels, and BRSR lists supply-chain management as a material risk-and-opportunity requiring supplier evaluation and support programmes.
risks.risk: Supply-chain disruption and its working-capital consequences

risks.note: Named as a key risk in MD&A alongside pricing and supply chain, notwithstanding that the Company is debt free and funds requirements from internal cash generation.

Growth in the industrial segments relevant to the Company remained muted with overall weakness in capex; the fabrication segment showed low growth and domestic market conditions were described as anemic, so earnings depend on a capital-goods cycle revival.
risks.risk: Demand cyclicality — muted industrial demand and weak capital expenditure

risks.note: Management expects strong volatility to continue in the face of developments in West Asia, and names geo-political developments, currency movements, tariffs and fiscal/monetary policies as the key drivers for the ongoing financial year.
risks.risk: Global macro and geo-political exposure — tariffs, policy and West Asia volatility

risks.note: Explicitly flagged in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' apart from the commercial risks; internal controls are evaluated against an emerging technology and regulatory landscape.
